title: Successor finite-sum comparison after pushforward
statement: For a morphism i : Z ⟶ X, natural number r, and ideal sheaf data I on Z, the pushforward of the (r+1)-fold finite biproduct of I is isomorphic to the biproduct of the pushforward of the r-fold finite biproduct and the pushforward of I.

source.place: Tag 01YF, final paragraph of lemma-coherent-filter; successor split-sum construction

proof.text: Let A be the constant family I.toModules on Fin (r+1), and B the constant family on Fin r. Define e from the coproduct of A to the binary biproduct of the coproduct of B and I.toModules by Sigma.desc: send index zero to biprod.inr, and each successor j.succ to Sigma.ι B j followed by biprod.inl. Its inverse is biprod.desc of Sigma.desc (fun j => Sigma.ι A j.succ) and Sigma.ι A 0. The two composites are identities by Sigma.hom_ext and biprod.hom_ext', followed by Fin.cases and the coproduct and biproduct inclusion equations. This also covers r=0, where there are no successor indices.

The existing Mathlib instance Scheme.Modules.pushforward.IsRightAdjoint gives preservation of binary products, and its Additive instance gives preservation of zero morphisms. Apply Mathlib preservesBinaryBiproducts_of_preservesBinaryProducts locally and compose (pushforward i).mapIso e with Functor.mapBiprod. This is the required isomorphism; no coherence, integralness, or closed-immersion hypothesis is used.
